perspective:
From Bradley Ochoa’s available perspective:

- He knows he is Bradley Ochoa, a Hispanic man with a high school education, working as a salesperson at a marketing firm. He knows Katherine Lasiloo as his colleague and the marketing manager; their professional relationship has been cordial but strained by differing views on sales and marketing strategy.
- In the first meeting, he prepared data and charts supporting traditional sales techniques. He told Katherine he appreciated her digital strategies but believed core sales would benefit more from traditional methods, presenting data from the last five campaigns. He heard Katherine say the market is evolving, digital outreach has potential, and ask how he reconciles his data with online engagement. He replied he was not suggesting abandoning digital marketing but felt proven methods were being sidelined. He heard Katherine propose analyzing the data together and integrating both approaches.
- After that meeting, he heard Katherine share recent digital campaign success stories with increased engagement and sales. He felt uncertain and asked her to explain how digital strategies are developed. He heard her explain targeting the right audience with the right message and offer to walk through analytics and decision-making. He admitted his doubts and interest in understanding digital. He heard her say it is important to adapt and evolve, and to dive deeper into the data.
- He then felt hopeful and proposed a joint strategy meeting to combine traditional and digital marketing. He heard Katherine agree, say combining strengths could lead to better results, and suggest scheduling brainstorming. He told her he was hopeful and appreciated collaboration. He heard her say she looked forward to leveraging each other’s strengths.
- After their joint meeting, he was excited and worked overtime on a board presentation draft integrating both their ideas. He told Katherine about the draft. He saw/heard her review it, call it comprehensive and well thought out, and praise his hard work. He said he was convinced the integrated approach would set them apart and wanted to nail the presentation. He heard Katherine express confidence and suggest a final fine-tuning review.
- After the presentation succeeded and the strategy was implemented, he felt grateful for his professional growth and collaboration. He thanked Katherine, saying he learned much. He heard her say it was a pleasure, the project came to fruition, and his openness made a successful partnership. He proposed regular strategy sessions; he heard Katherine agree, saying it would keep them on top of their game and market trends.

Not available to Bradley: Katherine’s private thoughts, her INTP personality, her bachelor’s degree, narrator-only summaries, and any events or information he did not directly observe or hear.
